6. (a) Titan is a moon of Saturn. The Titan-Sun distance is 9.3 times greater than the Earth-Sun distance.
(i) Show that the intensity of the solar radiation at the location of Titan is $16\ \text{W m}^{-2}$. [1]
(ii) Titan has an atmosphere of nitrogen. The albedo of the atmosphere is 0.22. The surface of Titan may be assumed to be a black body. Explain why the average intensity of solar radiation absorbed by the whole surface of Titan is $3.1\ \text{W m}^{-2}$. [3]
(iii) Show that the equilibrium surface temperature of Titan is about 90 K. [1]
(b) The mass of Titan is 0.025 times the mass of the Earth and its radius is 0.404 times the radius of the Earth. The escape speed from Earth is $11.2\ \text{km s}^{-1}$. Show that the escape speed from Titan is $2.8\ \text{km s}^{-1}$. [1]
(c) (i) The orbital radius of Titan around Saturn is $R$ and the period of revolution is $T$. Show that $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2 R^3}{GM}$ where $M$ is the mass of Saturn. [2]
(ii) The orbital radius of Titan around Saturn is $1.2 \times 10^{9}$ m and the orbital period is 15.9 days. Estimate the mass of Saturn. [2]
(d) The molar mass of nitrogen is $28\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.
(i) Show that the mass of a nitrogen molecule is $4.7 \times 10^{-26}$ kg. [1]
(ii) Estimate the root mean square speed of nitrogen molecules in the Titan atmosphere. Assume an atmosphere temperature of 90 K. [2]
(e) Discuss, by reference to the answer in (b), whether it is likely that Titan will lose its atmosphere of nitrogen. [1]
